source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.anchor: Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 on printed p. 34; Theorem 4.3, first part, printed pp. 35–36 / PDF pp. 47–48.

target: Exhibit a proper convex objective whose subgradients are 2-strongly monotone on their domain although that domain fails the midpoint chord bound. Prove the corresponding equivalence on a convex subset of supported points.

searched_existing: Extended-real convexity and properness; global subgradient domain; the existing strong convexity / quadratic support growth equivalence.
known_consumers: The concrete converse counterexample calls the support-carrier classification, the all-pairs monotonicity result and the midpoint failure.
Four concrete checks use an unsupported finite midpoint, distinct boundary normals with a sharp pairing, a scaled coordinate chart, and the zero-modulus absolute value example.
planned_consumers: Weighted entropy on the convex positive weighted simplex.
reuse_plan.decision_reason: Reuse the existing quadratic support-growth equivalence in both directions. The converse needs support at every point of a segment. The counterexample makes that missing hypothesis visible.
